{{Quote|I thought the Sith teachings that were active here had been contained. Apparently I was wrong.|[[Arca Jeth]]|audio=Krath1-DLOTS.flac|<ref name="darklordsA">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
The '''Krath''' were a [[Sith cult/Legends|secret society]] founded by aristocrats [[Aleema Keto|Aleema]] and [[Satal Keto/Legends|Satal Keto]] in the year [[3998 BBY]], in the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]].

==History==
{{Quote|I'll bet they don't even understand what they've unleashed... and that can make them all the more dangerous.|[[Cay Qel-Droma]]|<ref name="darklords1">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]]</ref>}}
The [[Sith cult/Legends|cult]] was formed by a clique of bored youths of the [[Tetan/Legends|Tetan]] nobility, led by Satal Keto, the heir-apparent, and his cousin Aleema. They named the cult after a [[Krath (mythology)|magician-god]] from the fairy tales of their childhood. For some time, the Krath secret society was of little note and played no major part in Tetan [[Politics/Legends|politics]]. All this changed shortly after the [[Freedon Nadd Uprising|Naddist Uprising]] on [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]]. The catalyst for this change was the influence of the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of the former [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Freedon Nadd]], who took an active interest in Satal and Aleema. He became their [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]] and progressed them quickly down the path to darkness, teaching them many of the secrets of the ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].

Fuelled by the ambition of the dark side, the young aristocrats began plotting their rise to power. Aleema and Satal engineered a [[Political uprising of the Empress Teta system|military and political coup]] in [[3997 BBY]], encasing [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Keto]] in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and [[Death/Legends|murdering]] all nobles and guildsmen opposing them. They created a new order on Empress Teta, replacing the previous governmental institutions with the monolithic rule of the Krath, based on the ruthless oppression of all dissent. A minor civil war broke out, as certain Tetan factions chose to rebel, but the Krath proved victorious thanks to Aleema's [[Sith sorcery/Legends|magical]] [[Mind trick/Legends|talents]], despite an [[Battle of Koros Major|attempt to intervene]] made by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].
[[File:SinisterSatal.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Co-founder, Satal Keto.]]

Fearing to lose the initiative, the Krath then seized the opportunity when the Jedi [[Conclave at Deneba|assembled en masse]] on [[Deneba/Legends|Deneba]], sending in [[Krath war droid/Legends|Krath war droids]]&mdash;powerful war [[Droid/Legends|droids]] designed for the task of slaying [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]&mdash;disguised as [[Service droid/Legends|servant droids]]. These [[Battle of Deneba|attacked]] the Jedi, killing [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Arca Jeth]]. This in turn made his [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]], [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]], determined to [[Mission to Empress Teta|infiltrate]] and destroy the cult.

However, Aleema came to know of Qel-Droma's intentions. Against the advice of Satal, she inducted the powerful young Jedi into the Krath, sensing his great [[The Force/Legends|Force]] potential. She eventually succeeded in converting him to the dark side, making use of her womanly wiles. The jealous Satal then attempted to have the rogue Jedi [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]], but he was himself [[Duel in the Iron Citadel (Satal Keto)|killed]] by Qel-Droma, who took his place as co-ruler and [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] of the Krath.

Shortly thereafter, the planet was visited by [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], who desired to destroy those who could potentially impede his own ascension to that of Dark Lord of the Sith. To this end, he [[Duel in the Iron Citadel (Exar Kun)|attacked]] the two [[darksider]]s, but was interrupted by the spirit of the millennia-old Dark Lord [[Marka Ragnos]], who advised them to ally instead of competing. Thus was formed the new [[Brotherhood of the Sith]], with Exar Kun as Dark Lord. The Krath&mdash;under the rule of newly-christened [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] Qel-Droma&mdash;became an integral part.

This signaled the beginning of the true greatness of the Krath. Within six months, the Tetans had conquered large territories and imposed several defeats on the now-strained Republic military. Qel-Droma's alliance with the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] led by [[Mandalore the Indomitable]] further strengthened the cult's influence.
[[File:Aleema.jpg|thumb|right|120px|Co-founder, Aleema Keto.]]

During this same period, the Krath order constructed a number of temples upon many of the worlds they invaded and seized during the [[Krath Holy Crusade]] of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. Such temples were renowned for their extraordinarily deep taint by dark side energies, and the guards fortunate enough to have been chosen for duty at these temples were granted the use of [[Krath Holy Battle Suit|Holy Battle Armor]], which only served to increase their reputation as fanatics. Many cynics, however, dismissed such fervor, noting that guard duty was oftentimes the safer course of action when compared to the casualty rates wrought by participating in the Krath's numerous military slave raids.

However, as its military campaign met increasing and determined Republic and Jedi resistance, the Krath/Sith alliance began to fall apart due to internal tensions; Aleema began a campaign of more or less open infighting, causing Qel-Droma's capture by the Jedi and murdering his Tetan supporters. Once freed by Kun, the rogue Jedi retaliated by sending Aleema on the [[Battle of Kemplex Nine|mission]] that would prove to be her doom. When Qel-Droma was [[Sever Force/Legends|eliminated]] by the Jedi [[Nomi Sunrider]] and Kun was defeated by a combined Jedi armada and presumed dead, there was no one left to lead the Krath, and the cult quickly fell apart from internal strife.

Those few Krath that survived the end of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] were scattered across the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], mainly in the regions around [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Some Krath eventually joined old [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] settlements, while others continued to exist on their own, delving into depths of the dark side. During the following decades, [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] forces occasionally clashed with these isolated pockets, who no longer had the benefit of ancient Sith teachings or access to the technology left behind in the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]].<ref name="KOTORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

During the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], a proxy conflict between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], some riddled ancient scrolls were discovered, presumably made by Krath cultists. Eventually, someone decided to solve the riddles and find what was written in the scrolls.<ref name="ARCH">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Archaelogy|Riddles of the Krath}}</ref>

[[Sebban Keto]] would later quietly re-establish the Krath in [[Cinnagar/Legends|Cinnagar]], several thousand years after the deaths of his ancestors.<ref name="Byss">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050414planet2|series=Byss and the Deep Core|text=Part 2: Empress Teta}}</ref> [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] studied the Krath teachings in his search for mastery over the dark side. [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] learned about the Krath from the [[Tedryn Holocron]].<ref name="endnotes">[[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]]</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Krath_warrior_and_droid.jpg|thumb|right|230px|A Krath war droid follows a Krath warrior into battle]]
The Krath were an unusual combination of direct influence from Sith spirits and reclaimed Sith learning. None of the early Krath received formal Sith training. Instead, they pieced together techniques from artifacts and occasional input from powerful Sith spirits, learning how to use ancient Sith amulets, project massive and destructive Sith illusions, and wield [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith sorcery]]. Female members of the Krath Cult were called [[Krath Death Witch|Death Witches]].<ref name="KOTORCG" /> Like their founders, Krath cultists generally had significant skill in mental illusion. Commonly, they also demonstrated aptitude in the handling and use of dark side artifacts, such as [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith talismans]] and [[Sith sword|alchemical weapons]].

==Behind the scenes==
[[Chris Avellone]] disclosed that the Krath did not appear in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'' because of how it would be bad in [[Wikipedia:French language|French]], even though he was unaware of what was the issue exactly.<ref name="Avellone">{{WebCite|url=http://forums.obsidianent.com/index.php?showtopic=25285&st=0&p=189305&|text=The two diplomates {{=}} sith lords???, Reeeally stretchin it here...|author=[[Chris Avellone]]|date=2004-11-17|work=[[Obsidian Entertainment]]'s [https://web.archive.org/web/20071011081537/http://forums.obsidianent.com/index.php?act=idx official forum]|quote=There are no Krath in the game or mentioned in the game. The reasons for this are pretty simple - apparently, while it was okay in TOJ and K1 (I believe), the word "Krath" seems to mean something pretty bad in French. I have no idea what it is, but it was sufficient to flush it from the game.|archivedate=20071013164203|nolive=1}}</ref> It is possible that this is because the word "Krath" sounds similar in French to the word "crasse", meaning "a layer of dirt" or even "mediocrity" in its literary meaning.<ref name="French">{{WebCite|url=https://www.larousse.fr/dictionnaires/francais/crasse/20242|text=Définitions : crasse, crasses|work=the [[Wikipedia:Éditions Larousse|Dictionnaire de français Larousse]]|archivedate=20250318172817}}</ref>
